identity.title: A Comparison of the Stellar, CO, and Dust-continuum Emission from Three Star-forming HUDF Galaxies at z ∼ 2

paper_type_evidence.quote: We probe the dust and molecular gas using subarcsecond Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array observations of the 1.3 mm continuum and CO line emission, respectively

coordinates.value: RA/Dec partly given (e.g. :32:34.44, :46:59.8 for ALPS.1; hours/degrees truncated in the text)

distance_source.value: CO redshifts; cosmology H0=70, OmegaM=0.3, OmegaL=0.7

question.value: How do the spatial extents (half-light radii) of stellar, CO and dust-continuum emission compare in three massive main-sequence-like HUDF galaxies at z~1.4-2.7, and are their kinematics rotation-dominated?

evidence.quote: we test how the spatial extent (quantified by the half-light radii) of dust continuum, CO and rest-frame optical emission compare for three extended, MS galaxies at $z\sim 2$.

analysis_steps.goal: Image Band 6 continuum and Band 3 CO

method.value: Pipeline-calibrated data concatenated and imaged with tclean (mosaic); moment-0 from single-channel image across line

evidence.quote: we create a single-channel image over the extent of the line emission

validation.value: Compared moment-0 maps with 50 and 100 km/s cube-derived maps

evidence.quote: We compare these moment-0 maps to maps obtained from 50 and 100 $\ensuremath{\rm{km}\, \rm{s}^{-1}}$ data cubes

analysis_steps.goal: Measure total flux densities, CO luminosities, gas and dust masses

method.value: Residual-scaling flux in circular apertures; L'CO via Solomon+1992; molecular masses via metallicity-based alpha_CO; dust masses from optically thin MBB

evidence.quote: we assume that the dust emission is optically thin and can be modeled by a modified blackbody
circular apertures of $1{\ooalign{{$.$}\cr{$''$}}}5,~ 2''$ and $1{\ooalign{{$.$}\cr{$''$}}}5$ for ALPS.1, 2 and 3, respectively

assumptions.value: T_dust = 25 K, beta = 1.8, kappa_850um = 0.77 cm^2/g, factor 1.36 for He

evidence.quote: taking $\kappa_{{\nu}_{850 \mathrm{\mu m}}} = 0.77\, \mathrm{g^{-1}cm^2}$ (cite: 1984ApJ...285...89D) and $\beta=1.8$

validation.value: Compared to ASPECS LP and Dunlop+2017 flux densities

evidence.quote: We compare the flux densities measured here (Table [2](#tab:derived_prop)) to those derived using the ASPECS LP data only.

analysis_steps.goal: SED fitting for stellar mass, SFR

method.value: MAGPHYS high-z with Battisti+2019 adaptation (ALPS.1, 3) and AGN version (ALPS.2)

evidence.quote: for ALPS.2 we apply the adapted version of that accounts for a contribution by AGN to the dust heating

assumptions.value: Chabrier IMF; 0.3 dex uncertainty floor on M* and SFR

evidence.quote: we adopt an uncertainty floor on the stellar masses and SFRs of $\pm\sim0.3$ dex
we quote the median values with uncertainties representing the 16th and 84th percentiles

method.value: Image-plane GALFIT Sersic fits in 4 arcsec region (n free for F160W, n=1 for CO/dust); uv-plane fits with uvmultifit and GILDAS uv_fit as cross-check; ALPS.3 upper limits from Gaussian deconvolution

evidence.quote: We therefore keep the Sérsic index as a free parameter when fitting the F160W emission but fix the Sérsic index to match an exponential profile ($n=1$) for the CO and dust emission.

key_parameters.value: PA and inclination within ±10 deg, centres within ±0.2 arcsec of van der Wel values

evidence.quote: constrain the source centres to vary by $\pm\, 0{\ooalign{{$.$}\cr{$''$}}}2$

fitting.value: GALFIT chi-square; uncertainties from fits to simulated maps

evidence.quote: We therefore quote uncertainties based on the distribution of best-fit values for fits to simulated maps.

validation.value: Simulated recovery tests; uv vs image-plane comparison

evidence.quote: We perform multiple tests to check to what extent we can recover the source sizes

method.value: Qubefit thin exponential disk 3D model fit with MCMC to 50 km/s cubes; Mdyn = v^2 r/G within 2 r_1/2 and 6 r_d

We fit the model cube to regions of 3$''$ diameter

findings_qualitative.value: CO emission is at least 30% more compact than rest-frame optical in all three; dust is more compact for ALPS.1 and 3 but similar in extent for ALPS.2

evidence.quote: for all three galaxies the CO emission appears $\gtrsim 30\%$ more compact than the stellar emission.

claims.hypothesis: CO and dust are more compact than stars in MS galaxies at z~2
claims.experiment: Sersic fits to ALMA CO, 1.3 mm and HST F160W maps
claims.result: CO >=30% smaller than F160W in all three; dust smaller in ALPS.1 and 3, similar in ALPS.2
claims.finding: Gas and dust are generally more compact than stars, though one source shows extended dust

evidence.quote: for the $z=1.6$ galaxy, the dust and stellar emission have similar spatial extents.

claims.experiment: Qubefit 3D modelling and PV diagrams of CO
claims.finding: All three consistent with rotation-dominated disks

evidence.quote: find that all three have kinematics consistent with a rotation-dominated disk.

why_this_data.value: CO- and dust-bright sources with extended optical sizes selected from ASPECS LP, requiring CO brightness to resolve in ~5 h

evidence.quote: We required the sources to be CO-bright in order to resolve their emission

limitations_admitted.value: Low S/N and resolution prevent multi-component decomposition and free Sersic index for CO/dust; sizes uncertain

evidence.quote: does not allow us to decompose the data into multiple components
